# dsh-model-show

The composer's model selector in DSH Web shows **Provider/Model** instead of a bare model name, so
t

he picked model always names the provider it came from — and nothing else about the selector
changes

e picked model always names the provider it came from — and nothing else about the selector
changes.
| | Composer trigger |

| Before | `Example Chat · High` |
| After | `Example Provider/Example Chat · High` |

*Above: provider `OpenCode Zen`, model `DeepSeek V4.1 Flash`; the trailing `Default` is the
thinking
-effort suffix DSH already appends.*

- **Only the trigger text changes.** The provider prefix comes from your own model configuration
(`d

isplayName`) — no hard-coded vendor list.
- **Dropdown and search stay native.** Rows remain plain m

t-in release badge survives** (`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` → `1017`) and keeps following
whatever the runn

ing DSH build ships.
- **Other plugins decorating the same label are rendered too**, each in its own

bounded box behind
an error boundary (v1.0.4).
- **No settings, no network, no telemetry.** It read
s the catalog DSH already has.
## Requirements

- DSH `>= 0.2.2-rc.1 < 0.2.3-0`, `web` client platform.
- The built-in model selection plugin (`@dee

pseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-model-selection`) must stay
enabled — this plugin reuses its `modelDirectorie

s` service and only shadows the composer seat.
The built-in label plugin (`…deepseek-model-label-101

7`) must stay enabled too; it draws the badge.
- Provider names are whatever your configuration decl
ares (`displayName`), e.g. `Example Provider`.
## Install
**Plugin market** — search the npm package name `dsh-model-show`, install, enable.
**Desktop CLI** (the reserved `desktop` profile is managed only by the app's own CLI):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

From GitHub or a local directory, replace the package name with `github:<user>/dsh-model-show` or
`"

C:\path\to\dsh-model-show"`. **Update** with an explicit version
(`add dsh-model-show@<version>` — s

ee releases; the registry `latest` can lag behind rc builds); **remove** with
`plugin --profile desk
top remove dsh-model-show`.
**Let the agent do it** — `plugin_manager`, `action: install_bundle`, `target` = package directory.
## In effect / off again
| Action | Effect |
| Install, enable or disable from the plugin UI or market | DSH recomposes the tree in place; with H

MR present (the Desktop build ships it) it applies **without a restart** |
| `dsh plugin … add` from

a shell, or hand-editing the profile | Disk-level change — restart once |
| Disable the plugin | Th
e slot entry is disposed and the **built-in seat takes over**: the trigger returns to the plain mode
l name, no leftovers |

If DSH ever answers “restart required” after a UI action, it is one of four documented reasons
(pack
age moved, host module touched, unmanaged plugin, module comparison) — none apply here.
## What it does
- **Trigger** — `Example Chat` → `Example Provider/Example Chat` (plus `· High` when the model has a

thinking effort).
- **Badge** — the built-in decorator matches the model name literally, so the unt

ouched catalog name
is kept beside the prefixed one and the decorator is replayed with it. The prefi

x shows once and
the badge keeps tracking DSH; it is never hard-coded.
- **Menu, search, ARIA** — ro

ws keep the plain name, search matches plain names only, and the ARIA
label mirrors the visible `Pro

name, search matches plain names only, and the ARIA
label mirrors the visible `Provider/Model` text.
## Why it cannot freeze the composer
`conversation.input.model` is a `single` slot: exactly one entry renders, and this plugin registers
at `priority: -1` so it shadows the built-in seat. DSH only injects a `renderSlot` face into entries
that declare children, and the child label slot may be declared only once (by the built-in seat) —
so the plugin composes that child slot itself:

- every registration is **mounted** with `createElement`, so a hook component keeps its own hooks;
-

every mount sits behind an **error boundary** — a render-phase throw from a third-party decorator
b

lanks that box only (the failure mode that used to freeze the menu with an empty log);
- every mount

sits in a **bounded box** (`min-width: 0`, `max-width: 100%`, `overflow: hidden`,
ellipsis), so a s

elf-contained pill cannot blow up the trigger;
- the **label body is DSH's own decorator** (locale p

refix `deepseek-model-label`); anything else is
appended beside it instead of dropped.

Side effect: those extra decorations also appear in the dropdown rows — the platform renders that
sl

ose extra decorations also appear in the dropdown rows — the platform renders that
slot per row too.
## FAQ

**Menu rows don't show the provider — a bug?** No. Only the trigger is rewritten, so grouping and
se
arch stay predictable.

**Badge gone?** Enable the built-in `…deepseek-model-label-1017` plugin; the badge is a replayed
dec
orator, not a string this plugin prints.

**Market card says host requirement unknown?** The curated catalog fills its `npm` field from the
re

gistry on its own schedule; once it has, the card shows the version and `engines.dsh` and installs
f

schedule; once it has, the card shows the version and `engines.dsh` and installs
from the registry.
[该节后续省略]
## Privacy
No network requests, no telemetry. It reads only what DSH exposes (the session's model catalog, the
locale dictionaries, the slot registry) and never writes your catalog, credentials or settings. The
published package is 12 files: code, locales, icon, screenshot, patch, licence/notice, readmes.
## Known limitations
- `lib/client.js` is a vendored copy of the built-in bundle, so it still relies on the browser modul

e
table's `dsh-client-ui-primitives`, `cordis` and `dsh-client-store` (declared in
`dsh.client.exter

nal`). A future refactor of the built-in selector can invalidate it; `engines.dsh`,
the vendoring sc

ript and the test suite are the three guards.
- The control reuses the built-in implementation, incl

uding its `min(360px, 45cqw)` trigger width: a
long `Provider/Model` is ellipsised, never wrapped.
-

The vendored bundle keeps the built-in plugin's full service list on purpose — the seat resolves
it

s catalog through the consuming context, and trimming the list makes the first render after
launch t

hrow and the seat silently retire.
- No settings: the format is fixed as `Provider/Model`.
- Third-p
arty decorations also render in the dropdown rows, which can look noisy in a long list.
